PROBLEM STATEMENT 
Smart Campus Multi-Agent AI System 
Background 
Educational institutions today rely on multiple disconnected platforms for academics, placements, examinations, 
clubs, events, library services, hostel management, grievances, and administrative processes. Students and 
faculty often spend significant time switching between these systems to find information, complete tasks, or 
access essential services. 
With the rapid advancement of Autonomous AI Agents, campuses have an opportunity to move beyond 
traditional chatbots toward intelligent systems capable of reasoning, planning, collaborating, and taking actions 
on behalf of users. 
Your challenge is to design and develop a Multi-Agent AI System that acts as a unified smart campus assistant, 
capable of understanding complex user requests, coordinating specialized AI agents, retrieving institutional 
knowledge, and autonomously executing tasks across multiple campus services. 
The focus of this challenge is not on building another chatbot. Instead, participants are expected to demonstrate 
agentic AI through autonomous planning, multi-agent collaboration, reasoning, memory, and tool usage. 
The Challenge 
Build a working proof-of-concept Multi-Agent AI System where multiple specialized AI agents collaborate to 
solve real-world campus problems. 
Your solution should include an Orchestrator Agent (or equivalent coordination mechanism) that intelligently 
routes tasks to one or more specialized agents. These agents should collaborate to complete user requests by 
retrieving information, reasoning over multiple steps, invoking tools or APIs, and generating meaningful 
responses. 
Participants are encouraged to think beyond simple question answering and demonstrate how AI agents can 
autonomously plan, coordinate, and execute workflows.

Illustrative User Workflows 
Example 1 
“I’m a third-year CSE student. Am I eligible for the Google internship? If yes, register me for tomorrow’s placement 
workshop, add it to my calendar, and remind me one hour before the event.” 
– Orchestrator understands intent 
– Placement Agent checks eligibility 
– Knowledge Agent retrieves placement policy 
– Events Agent registers the student 
– Calendar Agent schedules the event 
– Notification Agent creates reminder 
– Final response returned to user 
 
Example 2 
“Summarize the examination regulations, calculate my attendance eligibility, and draft an email requesting permission 
for a makeup exam.”

Functional Requirements 
Your solution should demonstrate more than four of the following: 
• Natural language understanding 
• Multi-agent collaboration 
• Autonomous task planning 
• Agent-to-agent communication 
• Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) 
• Tool / Function Calling 
• Workflow orchestration 
• Personalized recommendations 
• Context-aware conversations 
• Memory across interactions 
• End-to-end workflow execution 
• Error handling and graceful fallback mechanisms 
Non-Functional Requirements 
Solutions should aim to demonstrate: 
• Modular architecture 
• Scalable agent design 
• Low-latency responses 
• Secure handling of user information 
• Reliable workflow execution 
• Clean and intuitive user experience 
• Well-documented architecture

Dataset & Integrations 
Participants are NOT expected to integrate with actual institutional systems. Solutions may use: 
• Mock APIs 
• JSON datasets 
• CSV files 
• SQLite / PostgreSQL databases 
• Sample institutional documents 
• Public datasets 
• Simulated campus services 
The emphasis is on AI reasoning and autonomous workflows, not enterprise integrations. 
Mandatory AI Components 
Every solution should include at least three of the following: 
• Multi-Agent Architecture 
• Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) 
• Function / Tool Calling 
• Autonomous Planning 
• Agent Memory

What We Are Looking For 
We are looking for solutions that move beyond traditional chatbots. Successful submissions should demonstrate 
how multiple AI agents can intelligently collaborate to understand user intent, retrieve relevant knowledge, 
interact with tools, make informed decisions, and execute meaningful workflows with minimal user 
intervention. 
Creativity is encouraged. Participants are free to define their own agent architecture, workflows, and 
implementation approach while addressing the core challenge of building an intelligent Smart Campus Multi-
Agent AI System. 
Expected Outcome 
At the end of the 24-hour hackathon, teams should present a functional proof-of-concept that showcases how 
Autonomous Multi-Agent AI Systems can transform campus experiences by enabling intelligent assistance, 
collaborative problem-solving, and workflow automation. The emphasis is on demonstrating innovation, 
practical AI engineering, and real-world impact through agentic systems rather than building a feature-complete 
campus platform.
